name: crime_type_key_raw_bytes
description: CQ23 (crime 7 'Other value types'): the name key 0x8A416B2E and the icon key 0xAA12FCB1 are read as the first 12 bytes of the value's data, three little-endian u32, whatever the element type; nothing is converted. The spec's worked examples: the shipped Generic key stored as the u16 array [0x960B, 0x2026, 0x4AE0, 0x0A55, 0xA698, 0xEA5E] gives G = 0x0A554AE0, I = 0xEA5EA698 (0x60 -> 'Generic'); the f32 array [0, 1, 2] gives G = 0x3F800000, I = 0x40000000 (0x61); the string 'ABCDEFGHIJKL' gives G = 0x48474645, I = 0x4C4B4A49 (0x62). [choice] (CQ23, recommended) A value with fewer than 12 data bytes is missing: the u8 array [1, 2, 3] has 3 bytes, so no lookup (converting element by element would ask for (0x2026960B, 2, 3)) and the inline name wins (0x63). The icon key: a u16 array [1, 0, 2, 0, 3, 0] gives (1, 2, 3) (0x64); two u32 (8 bytes) are missing, so the icon is the default (0, 0, 0) (0x65). Hand-derived from the spec's table.
